answer: Unique pumps beat cheap keys. Admit an earning address only as sole lessee of a serialized Archimedes screw on a named oasis intake, hashing that spiral pitch at install so a swapped rotor fails. When the seed appears, that shaft must post a signed encoder trace—the lift signal—embedding the seed while the window is open. One screw finishes one certified lift in time, so each extra identity buys and crews its own pump. Shop math, not a bid: $1,200 to stand the screw up and $30 per witnessed cycle; eighty clones spend $96,000 plus $2,400 that round.
